subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: What policy snapshot must synchronous exec authorization reads observe while the same process owns an async approvals write lock?
rationale: Choosing between the previous committed policy, the writer's validated next snapshot, or fail-closed behavior defines an authorization and revocation-ordering contract that cannot safely be inferred from the current patch.

options.title: Use a transaction snapshot
options.body: Serve synchronous readers a validated process-local committed snapshot while the async writer owns the lock, preserving availability without reading the file outside serialization.

options.title: Remove the sync contention path
options.body: Refactor the affected async callers so they carry prepared policy state forward and never invoke a synchronous store read while holding the writer lock.

options.title: Accept stale lockless reads
options.body: Document and explicitly approve stale authorization decisions during same-process writes, with live revocation and Windows copy-fallback proof.

recommendation.title: Use a transaction snapshot
recommendation.body: Serve synchronous readers a validated process-local committed snapshot while the async writer owns the lock, preserving availability without reading the file outside serialization.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history most directly covers the core exec-approval security model and authorization invariants.
